candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits in this table are instream waste-concentration derivations versus direct effluent limits affects which numeric value is compared to reported discharge measurements and whether effluent concentration (Ce) inputs are required to establish an applicable limit.

The acute aquatic instream limit is expressed as a formula tied to effluent concentration; different readings of the multiplier or its applicability change the calculated enforceable numeric limit used for exceedance comparison.

Method quantitation limits govern whether reported values below detection can be numerically compared to criteria; interpretation of MQL relative to a measured or missing result changes limit-exceedance evaluation (A) and how sub-quantitation or no-result evidence is classified (C).

The parenthetical (P) may denote provisional or specially designated criteria; whether such limits are enforceable for compliance comparison changes which numeric limit applies to nickel dissolved measurements.

The (P) designation may mark provisional criteria with different enforceability; treating it as enforceable versus informational changes the applicable selenium dissolved limit and exceedance outcome.
Interpretation of (P) as provisional or conditionally applicable affects whether the listed thallium dissolved criteria are used as enforceable discharge limits.

This row defines a sulfate-conditioned selenium criterion; whether sulfate exceeds 500 mg/l determines which limit applies (A) and whether monitoring or evaluation against this alternate criterion was required for a given period (B).

candidates.computation_change_reason: Multiple parallel numeric criteria columns are listed for each pollutant; which column governs the enforceable discharge limit depends on receiving-water use designations and permit context, changing the limit selected for comparison.

Sentinel values of 1E+100 appear throughout the criteria columns; reading them as no applicable numeric criterion versus a literal limit changes whether a compliance comparison is possible for that pollutant and use class.

Pollutant form (dissolved versus total) determines which row's criteria apply; matching the wrong form to a reported mercury measurement selects a different numeric limit (e.g., acute aquatic 1.4 µg/l versus total-mercury values).
Total and dissolved mercury rows carry different criteria across columns; parameter matching affects which enforceable limit is used when comparing reported measurements.

This row has blank effluent-concentration fields while still listing criteria; interpretation of whether a calculable instream or effluent limit exists affects limit applicability (A) and whether missing supporting concentration data leaves the case unresolved (C).

The Need TMDL column is uniformly N/A; whether N/A means no TMDL-driven limit or obligation applies versus incomplete information affects selection of applicable limits (A) and whether TMDL-related monitoring or special study requirements exist (B).
